newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's key share index rebounds to close flat.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's key share index rebounds to close flat.

text.p: Singapore's key share index finished flat on Tuesday as investors stayed on the sidelines ahead of a U.S. decision on whether to raise interest rates.
Most brokers expected, and had discounted, a 25 basis points rise by the Federal Open Market Committee later on Tuesday.
"But it may trigger another round of fears that the interest rate will fall further before the end of the year," said an institutional dealer with a foreign brokerage.
Lack of interest was reflected in a thin market volume of 74.72 million shares. Gainers beat losers by 148 to 124.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index rose a marginal 3.48 points to 2,160.27.

The SES Electronics index posted a firm 2.32 percent increase with a 1.78 point rise to 78.37 on Trade and Industry Minister Yeo Cheow Tong's statement that an upturn for the electronics sector was likely in early 1997.

Creative Technology 50 shares soared Singapore $1.80 to S$7.75 when Merrill Lynch upgraded the stock to a "hold" from a "sell". There was also talk of takeover attempts by Samsung and Singapore Technologies Group.
Blue chips OCBC foreign and SIA foreign were among the losers.
